bench.button: How to pack bundles and gifts
bench.intro: What you see on a parcel that holds a bundle or a gift.

s1.p1: A bundle is split into the products you put in the box. You scan each one on its own. The "Bundle: ..." header shows how many components are already in the parcel.
s1.p2: A gift is an ordinary unit to scan, only marked. It covers a gift from a bundle and a gift from a promotion or added by hand. No prices or costs are shown here.
s1.p3: If a bundle component has no code to scan, the parcel closes only after a manual confirmation. Do not ship a bundle in parts.
s1.title: Bundle in the parcel

s2.p1: When you verify the last unit the parcel closes by itself, with no button. If it closed by mistake, reopen it and the units reset.
s2.title: Closing the parcel

bench.title: Packing bundles and gifts

detail.intro: How to read lines that cost the customer nothing or belong to a bundle, and what to do when a gift is missing.

s1.p1: A bundle is one line at the bundle price. Below it you see its components marked "in the bundle price". The packer gets the composition from the day of the order, so later changes to the bundle do not touch this order.
s1.p2: A 0.00 line. Click the tag to see where the gift came from, who pays for it and how it shows on the sales document.
s1.p3: A promotion in OpenLinker (with a link), a shop cart rule, a gift app in the shop or added by hand by an operator. You fund each one: the customer pays 0.00 and the cost shows at purchase price.
s1.title: Order lines

s2.p1: The order goes on without the gift. The decision is saved and the notice goes away. The promotion does not try again.
s2.p2: You can give another gift instead of the missing one. It works until the parcel is closed.
s2.title: When a gift is missing

s3.p1: The gift form is a tax decision. The most specific setting wins: the gift itself, then the sales channel, then the OpenLinker default. Every gift shows where its form came from. Own price shows the gift at a price you choose and takes that amount off the most expensive paid line, so the total does not change.
s3.title: Gift on the document

detail.title: Gifts and bundles in an order

list.intro: How OpenLinker shows goods the customer did not pay for separately on the orders list, and what to do about them.

s1.p1: The order has a 0.00 line. A promotion, a shop cart rule or an operator added it. The "With a gift" filter shows only these orders.
s1.p2: One order line is made of several products. The peek shows them under the bundle, marked "in the bundle price". A gift inside a bundle is marked separately.
s1.p3: A promotion was meant to add a gift but could not, for example because it is out of stock. The order goes on without it. Open it to skip the gift or add one by hand.
s1.title: Row marks

s2.p1: The button beside the filters turns this filter on with one click. The same one is under Filters, in Exceptions.
s2.p2: The numbers above the table are orders where something needs you: gift not added, shop rejected the gift, deadline passed.
s2.title: Filters

list.title: Gifts and bundles in orders

returns.intro: Returning one component of a bundle, and the decision about a gift the customer does not send back.

s1.p1: Tick the components that really came back. Only they go back to stock. The bundle stays one invoice line, and the refund hint follows the Allegro formula: paid minus what stays with the customer at full price. Nothing is filled in by itself.
s1.p2: If a component has no price or cost, it is not known what the returned part is worth. We block a partial return and say which component is missing something. You can always accept the whole bundle.
s1.title: Bundle on return

s2.p1: OpenLinker never deducts a gift by itself. Until you choose, the gift is "not decided yet". Deducting is a hint beside the refund amount, nothing is entered for you. Do it only when the offer terms say so.
s2.title: Gift on return

returns.title: Returns of bundles and gifts

stock.intro: A gift takes stock like any line, but has its own type so you can see how many were given away.

s1.p1: When a gift lands in an order its stock is reserved. Until the order leaves, the stock in the master system does not change.
s1.p2: When the parcel is shipped, the reservation becomes a stock change.
s1.p3: A cancelled order or one the shop refused releases the gift reservation. The stock returns to the pool.
s1.title: Type "Gift"

s2.p1: The movement peek shows the order and, if a promotion gave the gift, a link to it. A gift added by hand shows who added it.
s2.title: Where a gift comes from
